reporting for Debt collection, BPO, Insurance and Arrears; a new Property module; client TV links; a status page; supervisors held to their teams' calls; and faster message sending.

Property module (add-on): a Property hub with units, people and listings, a listing feed by file upload or signed webhook, a Property tab on the agent desk, property fields and lists, a listings report, dashboard and tile, and a guide and Academy lessons.

Debt collection: a Hold compliance report and a Collected against target report, wallboard tiles for forecast by month end, right-party contacts per hour, promise value today, targets and debit orders, and a money leaderboard. There are starter dashboards for the collections floor, the creditor view and the manager's month, and a money floor wallboard. Report rows and dashboard tiles open their accounts, and expected money now counts debit orders.

BPO module: contract service level by interval, credits at risk, billable time, cost per contact, client P&L and staffing against contract, with Account manager, Client board and BPO finance dashboards, contract tiles and an Account manager wallboard. Every figure opens its calls. The hub shows each contract's monthly value, staffing bands and cost per agent hour to BPO finance users only, and agents get a BPO tab on the desk with today's service level per client and their own handled and billable time.

Insurance: Sales to issue, Premium written, Cooling-off cancellations, Reinstatements and Policy movement reports, and persistency by agent, team, campaign, class or insurer with a 12 month checkpoint. There are monthly premium and policy targets, sales floor wallboard tiles and a premium leaderboard, Insurance sales floor and Insurer view dashboards, figures that open their policies, and My insurance figures on the agent desk.

Arrears: a Targets tab with collection targets shared with Debt collection, the agent's own figures on the desk's Arrears tab, and new reports over arrears accounts only: the contact funnel (a call to a guardian or co-tenant counts, split by who was reached), promise quality, expected money, bucket movement with the cure rate, cost to collect, recovery by billing period (at the due date and 30, 60 and 90 days on), and deposit cover for rent.

Client TV links: a wallboard or dashboard TV link can be tied to one client, such as a BPO client, a creditor or an insurer. It shows only that client's figures, never money, agent names or other clients.

Supervisors and their teams: a supervisor named on teams now sees only their teams' calls everywhere: call records and their export, call detail, live calls, recordings (including voicemail and screen recordings), the call library, transcripts, call translation and the call trace.

Top bar shortcuts: the Assistant, Setup health with its problem count, and Test a call are one click away in the top bar.

Status page: platform operators keep a public status page with components, a notice timeline and notices shown to the clients who use the affected components.

Faster sending: up to four messages go out at once, still in order within each conversation, with replies ahead of marketing messages. A message that fails before it is sent backs off and is marked failed instead of holding up its conversation.

Agent status from your platform: an integration can set an agent Ready or Not ready with a reason, read their status and get an agent.state_changed webhook, and the web phone keeps the agent signed in while its page is open.

Reply modes: a How replies were written report shows, per agent, queue or channel, how sent replies were written; the composer follows the queue's reply mode; and a channel set to the AI alone warns when the plan has no tickets.

Workforce: agents book their own seat from My shifts and managers rename seats on the seat map; working-time rules can differ per site, with a Kenya pack for the weekly rest day.

Freelancers: a new setting, off by default, decides whe"}
